facts.fact: The Interior Ministry's director-general of territorial administration (DGAT/DD) presented, at Diffa on 3 September 2026, the computerisation of communes and declaration centres and a sovereign platform for the Registre National d'État Civil as the ministry's short- and medium-term works.

The civil-status and identification reforms, including the planned computerisation of communes and declaration centres, are carried out under the WURI-Niger project with World Bank support, as the ANP reports on 3 September 2026; no domestic budget line is mentioned.

The DGAT/DD said on 3 September 2026 that modernisation of civil status is among the priorities of the Programme de la Refondation de la République 2025-2029, and listed the computerisation of communes and declaration centres and a sovereign Registre National d'État Civil platform among its works; the programme is not said to be costed.

On 3 September 2026 the Interior Ministry announced as planned, not yet done, the progressive computerisation of communes and declaration centres and the creation of a Registre National d'État Civil, following adoption of the civil-status ordinance and creation of the ANEI.
